title: Mitigate unexpected variant swap after capacity surge causing orphaned retries
creator: Asha Patel
description: Summary: During a capacity surge on 2026-02-27 we observed a wave of cross-region retries and a set of requests that were served with an unintended model variant. The immediate customer symptom was increased tail latency and a small spike in degraded responses. Root cause in brief: a policy recompute path reweighted variants while an inflight KV cache eviction sequence completed, leading to a race where the router recorded a new variant affinity but some backends still served the old variant, triggering orphaned retries and a transient fanout. This ticket collects follow-ups, mitigations, and rollout plan to prevent recurrence.
comments: 2026-03-01 — Asha Patel: Initial triage complete. Incident created (INC-2026-02-27-47). Traces show bursts of retries from the routing service coincident with a capacity autoscale event in eu-west-1. Grafana dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.example/d/obs/routing-retries?view=incident-2026-02-27

2026-03-02 — Markus Chen: Reproduced locally with a simulated capacity surge. Root cause hypothesis: policy recompute path does an in-memory weight rebuild and publishes a new affinity map before KV cache eviction completes; routers accept the new affinity and client retries fan out to variants that are still warming. Added temporary mitigation: increased interlock window between publish and affinity flip (hotfix: https://github.com/redwood-inference/routing/pull/8421).

2026-03-03 — SRE (Lina Morales): Deployed hotfix to staging and canary; observed elimination of the immediate fanout under load. However retrospective shows telemetry gaps: we lack a metric that ties variant-affinity-change events to in-flight KV state. Created proto-dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.example/d/obs/variant-affinity-telemetry

2026-03-05 — Eng Review: Trade-offs discussed. Options: (A) add synchronous confirmation from backends that variant is warmed before publishing affinity (higher latency during rollouts), (B) adopt optimistic publish with stronger circuit breakers to suppress cross-region fanout (lower rollout latency but more complex failure modes). Team consensus: implement (B) short term, and schedule (A) as a hardening task for runtime-1.22. Added task to add circuit-breaker heuristics and exponential backoff for cross-region retries.

2026-03-07 — QA (Ravi Desai): Test plan added. End-to-end test will simulate variant weight flips concurrent with KV eviction, validate no >3x retry multiplier and no servicing of mismatched variants post-ack. Test harness PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/test-harness/pull/129

2026-03-09 — Markus Chen: Implemented circuit-breaker and retry-suppression patch (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/routing/pull/8475). Also added a fast path to detect stale KV tokens on incoming requests and reject with controlled fallback to local cache. Canary rollout scheduled for 2026-03-11.

2026-03-11 — Canary notes (obs): Canary at 20% shows 78% reduction in cross-region retries and no observed mismatched-variant responses. Still seeing rare KV-staleness warnings logged; added additional guards to make logs actionable. Dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.example/d/obs/canary-variant-safety

2026-03-12 — Postmortem draft (Asha Patel): Action items enumerated below. Recommend follow-ups in next cycle: 1) Add variant-affinity↔KV-state telemetry (high priority). 2) Implement synchronous warm-confirmation for critical workflows (runtime-1.22). 3) Expand chaos tests in CI for simultaneous scale + policy recompute. 4) Update runbook to include manual circuit-breaker flip instructions and rollback playbook. Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.example/display/ENG/Variant+Swap+Incident+2026-02-27

2026-03-12 — PM review (Dana Ortiz): Reviewed action items and added customer communication note template. Suggested we prioritize alerting to customers with high SLA exposure; assigned to CS for outreach.
